exams.syllabus:
## BPSC CCE Prelims: General Studies (1 paper)

- **Questions:** 150 objective (MCQ)
- **Time:** 2 hours
- Prelims is a **screening test**; its marks are not added to the final merit.

### Topics

1. General Science
2. Current events of national and international importance
3. History of India and salient features of the history of Bihar
4. General Geography and geographical divisions of Bihar, and its major river systems
5. Indian Polity and Economy, including the economy of Bihar after independence
6. Indian National Movement and Bihar's role in it
7. General Mental Ability

> ⚠️ This is a sample syllabus. Always check BPSC's official notification before the exam.

exams.syllabus:
## UPSC CSE Prelims

| Paper | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| GS Paper I | 100 | 200 | 2 hours |
| CSAT (GS Paper II) | 80 | 200 | 2 hours |

CSAT is **qualifying** (33% needed). The cut-off is decided on GS Paper I. Wrong answers carry a **1/3 negative mark**.

### GS Paper I

- Current events of national and international importance
- History of India and the Indian National Movement
- Indian and World Geography: physical, social and economic
- Indian Polity and Governance: Constitution, political system, Panchayati Raj, public policy, rights issues
- Economic and Social Development: sustainable development, poverty, inclusion, demographics, social sector initiatives
- Environmental ecology, biodiversity and climate change
- General Science

### CSAT (Paper II)

- Comprehension
- Interpersonal skills, including communication skills
- Logical reasoning and analytical ability
- Decision making and problem solving
- General mental ability
- Basic numeracy (Class X level) and data interpretation

> ⚠️ Always check UPSC's official notification before the exam.

Exam Conducting Body	Bihar Staff Selection Commission (BSSC)
Exam Name	BSSC CGL 2026
Mode of Exam	Online
Vacancy	1883
BSSC CGL Exam Date 2026	July-August 2026
Total Marks	600

Selection Process Stages
The selection process follows a rigorous two-stage format: the Preliminary Examination and the Mains Examination. Candidates are shortlisted for the Mains in a 1:5 ratio.

BSSC CGL Prelims: Exam Pattern & Guidelines
The Preliminary stage acts as a qualifying filter. With a duration of 2 hours and 15 minutes, accuracy is key due to the negative marking scheme (1 mark deducted for every incorrect answer, while 4 marks are awarded for correct ones).

Subjects	No. of Questions	Marks

General Studies	50	200
General Science and Mathematics	50	200
Logical Reasoning/Mental Ability	50	200
Mains Exam Pattern

Qualifiers proceed to the Mains, which consists of two papers. Paper 1 is a mandatory Hindi language test, while Paper 2 covers core subjects.

Paper	Subjects	Marks
Paper 1	Hindi Language	400
Paper 2	General Studies, Science, Math, Reasoning	600

exams.name: Assistant Professor in Economics
exams.fullName: Assistant Professor & PGT Economics: UPESSC, all states, UGC NET
exams.description:
One place to prepare for **Assistant Professor (Economics)** and **PGT Economics** exams in every state, with UGC NET Economics as the base.

**Start with the subject "Start Here"**: it has the 5-day plan, the state-wise exam list (North India first), the book list and the formula sheet. Then go unit by unit: each unit has long notes with diagrams, a mind map and a solved practice test. "Current Economy 2026" has the Economic Survey, the Union Budget and state budgets.

⚠️ The countdown uses the reported UPESSC written exam date (19 Nov 2026). Check [upessc.up.gov.in](https://upessc.up.gov.in) for the official date.
exams.syllabus:
## Exam pattern: UPESSC Assistant Professor (Advt. 04/2026)

| Part | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Knowledge | 30 | 90 |
| Economics (subject) | 90 | 270 |
| **Written total** | **120** | **360** (3 marks each) |
| Interview | | 40 |

- Objective (MCQ), 2 hours. Reported negative marking: −1 for a wrong answer.
- Written exam: **19–20 November 2026** (as reported; confirm on [upessc.up.gov.in](https://upessc.up.gov.in)).

> ⚠️ Numbers above are collected from news and coaching sites on 4 Nov 2026. Always check the official notification.

## Economics syllabus (UGC NET Economics, code 01)

Most Assistant Professor exams (UPESSC, MPPSC, RPSC, HPSC, BPSC) follow this UGC NET syllabus closely. PGT exams use a simpler version of the same topics.

### Unit 1: Micro Economics
Theory of demand (utility, indifference curves, revealed preference, Slutsky), production and costs, market structures (perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly), game theory, factor pricing, general equilibrium and welfare economics, economics of information.

### Unit 2: Macro Economics
National income accounting, consumption and investment functions, Keynesian and classical models, IS–LM and IS–LM–BP, aggregate demand and supply, inflation and unemployment (Phillips curve), business cycles, rational expectations and new classical/new Keynesian ideas, money demand and supply.

### Unit 3: Statistics and Econometrics
Probability and distributions, sampling, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, OLS and the classical linear regression model, multicollinearity, heteroscedasticity, autocorrelation, dummy variables, simultaneous equations, time series basics, index numbers.

### Unit 4: Mathematical Economics
Sets, functions, differentiation and optimisation (constrained, Lagrange), matrices and input–output analysis, linear programming, difference and differential equations, game theory.

### Unit 5: International Economics
Trade theories (Ricardo, Heckscher–Ohlin, Stolper–Samuelson, Rybczynski, new trade theory), terms of trade, tariffs and quotas, balance of payments, exchange rate theories and regimes, open-economy macro (Mundell–Fleming), WTO and trade blocs.

### Unit 6: Public Economics
Market failure, public goods and externalities, public choice, theories of public expenditure, taxation (incidence, efficiency, optimal taxation), budget and deficits, public debt, fiscal federalism and Finance Commissions, GST.

### Unit 7: Money and Banking
Theories of money demand and supply, high-powered money and the money multiplier, RBI and monetary policy tools, inflation targeting, banking structure and reforms, financial markets, NBFCs, financial inclusion.

### Unit 8: Growth and Development Economics
Growth models (Harrod–Domar, Solow, endogenous growth), development theories (Lewis, big push, balanced vs unbalanced growth, dependency), poverty and inequality measures, human development, institutions.

### Unit 9: Environmental Economics and Demography
Environment as a public good, externalities and Pigouvian tax, Coase theorem, valuation methods, sustainable development, climate policy; demographic transition, population theories, census and NFHS data, migration.

### Unit 10: Indian Economy
Planning and NITI Aayog, agriculture, industry and services, economic reforms since 1991, poverty and unemployment, inflation, fiscal and monetary policy in India, external sector, recent Economic Survey and Budget.

exams.name: BPSC Mains (with Economics)
exams.fullName: BPSC Auditor, DSO, FAO and CCE Mains with Economics
exams.description:
Everything for **BPSC Mains** where **Economics** is a paper: **Auditor, District Statistical Officer (DSO), Financial Administrative Officer (FAO)** (Economics 300 marks, counted in merit) and **CCE** (optional). Includes Economics (theory notes + Bihar Economy), GS-I, GS-II, Essay and General Hindi.

Start with **"Start Here"** for the pattern and answer-writing rules.

⚠️ The countdown date is a placeholder. Update it from Admin when BPSC announces the next Mains date.
exams.syllabus:
## Auditor / DSO / FAO Mains

| Paper | Marks | Status |
|---|---|---|
| General Hindi | 100 | qualifying |
| General Studies I | 300 | merit |
| General Studies II | 300 | merit |
| **Economics** (or Commerce / Mathematics / Statistics) | **300** | **merit** |

## BPSC Mains (CCE): papers

| Paper | Marks | Status |
|---|---|---|
| General Hindi | 100 | qualifying |
| General Studies I | 300 | merit |
| General Studies II | 300 | merit |
| Essay | 300 | merit |
| Optional (Economics) | 100 (recent CCE cycles) | qualifying |
| Interview | 120 | merit |

### GS-I
1. Indian culture (with Bihar)
2. Modern history of India (with Bihar)
3. Current events of national and international importance
4. Statistical analysis, graphs and diagrams

### GS-II
1. Indian polity
2. Indian economy and geography of India (with Bihar)
3. Role and impact of science and technology in the development of India (and Bihar)

### Economics paper (300 marks in Auditor, DSO, FAO)
Part I: economic theory (national income, consumer and producer behaviour, markets, income and employment, distribution, money and banking, international trade, public finance). Part II: Indian economy and **Bihar economy** (planning, agriculture, industry, poverty, unemployment).

> ⚠️ Pattern details are collected from coaching sites (Nov 2026) and differ between sources. Confirm in the official notification on [bpsc.bihar.gov.in](https://bpsc.bihar.gov.in).
